slides.headline: Dancer? Strength is the missing piece
slides.sub: Why Pilates suits dancers who already have plenty of flexibility.

slides.title: Flexibility needs control
slides.body: Many dancers can reach end range easily but have less strength there. Pilates trains control through the full range, so extensions, balances and landings can feel steadier and more repeatable.

slides.title: Turnout from the hips
slides.body: Forcing turnout from the knees and feet can load them up. Side-lying work and reformer footwork help train the deep hip muscles, so more of your turnout comes from the hips.

slides.title: Feet and ankles that land well
slides.body: Rises, jumps and pointe work demand strong feet and calves. Footwork on the reformer, single-leg rises and slow lowering build capacity for long rehearsal days.

slides.title: Fit it around rehearsals
slides.body: One or two sessions a week is a good starting point, lighter in performance weeks and heavier in the off-season. The summer break is often a handy time to build strength before term.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain in one spot on the foot or shin that builds with jumping, a painful catch in the hip, or lower back pain with backbends is worth an assessment before training through it.

slides.headline: Build strength for the studio
slides.body: Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy starts with an assessment of your strength and control, then builds a program around your dance style. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Dancer? You've probably got the flexibility. Strength is often the missing piece. 🩰

Many dancers can reach end range easily but have less control once they're there. Clinical Pilates trains strength through the full range, which can help extensions, balances and landings feel steadier.

Side-lying work and reformer footwork help turnout come more from the hips, while single-leg rises build feet and calves for jumps and pointe work. One or two sessions a week is a good starting point, and the summer break is a handy time to build.

Pain in one spot on the foot or shin, a painful hip catch or back pain with backbends is worth an assessment first.
